newsitem.title: USA: BEFORE THE BELL - PLC slumps on FDA news.
newsitem.headline: BEFORE THE BELL - PLC slumps on FDA news.

text.p: Shares in PLC Systems Inc tumbled Tuesday on news the Food and Drug Administration (FDA) had rejected its laser system to treat chest pain, traders said.

Stock in the Franklin, Mass., company were trading at 15, down from a Monday close of 25-10/16. The stock was halted all day Monday pending the FDA's report on the system's merits, and resumed trade at 0813 EDT/1213 GMT Tuesday morning.
In a statement, the FDA said PLC had presented incomplete data and had little understanding of how the heart laser system worked.
Among other active stocks, Cyrix Corp was boosted by news it would merge with National Semiconductor Corp.
Shares in Cyrix were trading at 25-1/2, up from a Monday close of 23-1/16. They had been two points higher than the closing price in after-hours trade Monday.
National Semiconductor said after the markets' close it and Cyrix would merge in a stock swap worth $550 million. National Semiconductor shares were trading at 32-1/2, off a Monday close of 33-7/16.
Citicorp was trading at 126-1/2, up from a close of 124-11/16, and Swedish-American drugs group Pharmacia & Upjohn was at 36-1/2 from a closing price of 37-10/16.
Pharmacia presented a lower-than-expected second-quarter profit Tuesday, and said it still saw negative sales and earnings trends in the second half of the year.
Traders reported little activity in the pre-open market.
